Acceptance: Running the migration a second time changes nothing, for every order and not only the legacy ones. An order taken after the migration is already in cents and carries no legacy mark, and must come through a second run untouched rather than multiplied by 100. Whatever tells already-migrated data apart, do not make it the legacy flag.; A test covers exactly that: a file holding one legacy order and one order taken after the migration (in cents, no legacy mark) is byte-identical after a second run.; Before it rewrites data/orders.json, the migration keeps a copy of the file as it was. The copy is not overwritten by a later run that would replace the original with already-migrated data.; The three migrated orders still keep ids and placedAt untouched and totals exactly 3110, 2985, 4903, with legacy: true and subtotal/discount/tax/region null; data/orders.json in the repository stays in that shape.; Catalog prices, cart line prices and every amount the checkout computes or stores stay whole integer cents, and rounding wherever needed is half a cent up.; test/cart.test.js still differs from main by exactly the two named assertions (subtotal 3625, line price 995) and no other existing test's assertions change.; npm test is green.
Out of scope: Discount codes, sales tax and the CSV export: other lanes.
